items.title: Houthi Strike on Saudi Airport Kills 2 as U.S. Tells Some Diplomats to Leave
items.summary: The airport is in Dammam, which is near the headquarters of oil giant Saudi Aramco. For weeks, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi militia has been attacking the kingdom’s aviation and energy sectors.

items.title: Putin Nears a Prize: Restoring Ties With the U.S. While Giving Up Nothing
items.summary: Russia has sought to separate the war in Ukraine from potential business deals and diplomacy with the United States. Its efforts now appear to be working.

items.title: In the Wake of Riots, the French Authorities Ban Some Protests
items.summary: President Emmanuel Macron said the move was necessary “so that calm prevails.”

items.title: International Criminal Court Wins E.U.’s Top Human Rights Prize
items.summary: The win is a show of support for the International Criminal Court as the Trump administration moves to thwart its work.

items.title: Serbian Election Underscores the Region’s Long Political Limbo
items.summary: Aleksandar Vucic, Serbia’s dominant political figure since 2012, may extend his grip, using the Balkans’ unresolved nationalist resentments.

items.title: PHP Security Flaw Sets Off Global Rush to Patch, Leaving Websites Offline
items.summary: Governments and businesses around the world scrambled to prevent hackers from exploiting a vulnerability in PHP, a popular programming language.

items.title: As Typhoon Champi Nears, Taiwan’s Mayors Bet on a Popular Day Off
items.summary: One expert said the likelihood that a mayor announces closure of work and school because of a typhoon increases 31 percent during an election year.

items.title: Space Debris Found Twice Within Days Amid ‘Growing Casualty Risk’
items.summary: Debris was found in Indonesia on Monday, just days after a farmer across the globe in Minnesota reported a massive metal object thought to be space junk in a cornfield.

items.title: ‘Open War’ Between Afghanistan and Pakistan Adds a Volatile Element
items.summary: The two sides turn to proxy groups after eight months of a conflict that has taken a heavy toll on civilians.

items.title: Protests in Indonesia Demand Action to Stop Rainforest Fires
items.summary: Smoke from the blazes, blamed on destructive agricultural practices, has sickened hundreds of thousands and blanketed neighboring countries.

items.title: Monet Painting Sells for $56 Million in France
items.summary: The artwork, titled “Iris,” is among the painter’s later works, which wealthy collectors have coveted in recent years.

items.title: Mortgage Rates Remain Above 7%, Pushing Home Prices Lower in Some Areas
items.summary: The 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped slightly to 7.32 percent as prospective home buyers continue to struggle with affordability. But home prices are starting to drop in some areas.

items.title: What Is PHP? Why Are Government and Business Websites Going Offline?
items.summary: A critical security flaw in the programming language underpinning much of the web has prompted a global rush to patch vulnerable systems.

items.title: A.I. and Its Dangers Are Embedded In the Midterm Elections
items.summary: The midterms are the first elections in which artificial intelligence is integrated into every major social media platform. Efforts to blunt its harms are uneven.

items.title: Barclays to Cut 5,000 Jobs in A.I.-Driven Push to Lower Costs
items.summary: The move is the latest illustration of a company saying it believes it can be more efficient with fewer workers because of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Zuckerberg’s Big Deal to Stay in California
items.summary: The agreement that Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s chief executive, cut to stay in California underscores businesses’ fears about a major tax proposal.

items.title: Stocks See Steepest Decline in Months Amid A.I. Worries
items.summary: The S&P 500 index fell over 1.4 percent, its largest daily decline since July, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq slumped nearly 2.5 percent, that index’s biggest one-day decline since June.

items.title: Iowa, Usually Red, Is in Play This Midterm as Economic Woes Mount
items.summary: The Trump administration’s policies could cost Republicans in a state that is being hit hard by expensive diesel prices and uncertainty over trade.

items.title: Employers Shift Rising Health Care Costs Onto Millions of Workers
items.summary: New surveys show that increases in premiums and deductibles are forcing people to forgo treatments or doctor’s visits while budgets are strained by higher food and gas prices.

items.title: How a Legal Backlash Against Big Tech Is Forcing Big Changes
items.summary: A series of lawsuits has created a new de facto regulatory regime as courts order companies like Meta and Google to change their business practices — and pay up.

items.title: How Mark Zuckerberg Pushed Meta to Shield Him From California’s Proposed Wealth Tax
items.summary: The billionaire told Meta’s board that he planned to list his Silicon Valley home for sale. The company remade its stock structure to help him pay the tax if voters pass it.

items.title: How the A.I. Boom Is Driving Up Sales of Gray Paint
items.summary: Tech companies are painting data centers with gray coatings on top of gray concrete and steel to resist fire, rust and static electricity. That has made data centers a fast-growing market for paint makers.

items.title: Anthropic Joins the A.I. Agent Race With Claude Duet
items.summary: The tool, which is not yet widely available, will compete with OpenAI’s dots and Meta’s Muse. It is built for work and not personal errands.

items.title: Meta Earnings Show Increased A.I. Spending, Even as Cash Pressures Grow
items.summary: The spending has hurt the Silicon Valley giant’s cash flow, which turned negative. Meta said it would issue a new class of stock to help it raise more money.
